sentences.en: Let us be laid within thy bosom, Richard, and weigh thee down to ruin, shame and death.
sentences.zh: 让我们躺在你的胸膛里，理查，将你压向毁灭、耻辱与死亡。

sentences.en: Thy nephew's souls bid thee despair and die.
sentences.zh: 你侄儿们的灵魂在召唤你绝望并死去。

sentences.en: I can barely speak after that.
sentences.zh: 听了那个之后我几乎说不出话来。

sentences.zh: 纯粹是因为害怕，因为当然……

sentences.en: You told me...
sentences.zh: 你告诉过我……

sentences.en: So, welcome, everybody, to the rest of the history of you doing this podcast about the princess and the tower.
sentences.zh: 那么，欢迎大家收听关于你们制作这档关于公主与高塔播客的剩余历史。

sentences.en: Tom Holland has absolutely got me here under false pretenses, because he told me that he was going to do a devastating impersonation of a creepy boy.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德绝对是以虚假的借口把我骗到这里来的，因为他告诉我他要对一个令人毛骨悚然的男孩进行毁灭性的模仿。

sentences.zh: 他们确实是令人毛骨悚然的男孩。

sentences.en: I mean, I defy anyone to listen to that and not be terrified, scared out of their wits.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我敢打赌任何人听了那个都会吓得魂飞魄散、惊恐万状。

sentences.en: I can imagine even now that listeners are cowering behind the sofas or under their beds out of dread.
sentences.zh: 我甚至现在都能想象到听众们因为恐惧而蜷缩在沙发后面或床底下的样子。

sentences.en: That was wet.
sentences.zh: 那可真够潮湿的。

sentences.en: That was Fotherington to us.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说那就是福瑟林顿。

sentences.en: It wasn't.
sentences.zh: 才不是。

sentences.en: It was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 那太吓人了。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Despair.
sentences.zh: 绝望吧。

sentences.en: Hello, birds.
sentences.zh: 你们好，小鸟们。

sentences.en: Hello, Sky.
sentences.zh: 你好，天空。

sentences.en: Despair and die.
sentences.zh: 绝望而死。

sentences.zh: 太吓人了。

sentences.en: And they were, of course, the princes in the tower, Edward V and his younger brother, Richard of Shrewsby, who in Shakespeare's play, Richard III,
sentences.zh: 他们当然就是塔中的王子，爱德华五世和他的弟弟什鲁斯伯里的理查，在莎士比亚的戏剧《理查三世》中，

sentences.en: appear to him on the eve of the Battle of Bosworth, along with the ghosts of everybody else that Richard has murdered.
sentences.zh: 他们在博斯沃思战役前夕出现在他面前，同行的还有理查谋杀过的所有人的鬼魂。

sentences.en: Or has he, yes.
sentences.zh: 或者他真的杀过吗？是的。

sentences.en: Well, in Shakespeare's play, yes, he has.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在莎士比亚的戏剧里，是的，他确实杀过。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no question about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: Okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: Of course he has in Shakespeare's play.
sentences.zh: 在莎士比亚的戏剧里他当然杀过。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: And it's actually the second quotation from Richard III that's featured in recent weeks,
sentences.zh: 这实际上是最近几周出现的第二句《理查三世》的台词，

sentences.en: because we also had one from Clarence's dream before Richard murders him by having him dunked in a butt of Marmsy on Bart Van Lee's sensational episode about the Dukes of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 因为在巴特·范·李关于勃艮第公爵的轰动一时的节目中，我们也听过克拉伦斯在理查将他浸入马姆齐甜酒桶谋杀之前的梦境片段。

sentences.en: So this is, we've moved from Burgundy back to England.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，我们已经从勃艮第回到了英格兰。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the question that we're asked, well, actually, the theme is princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们被问到的问题，哦不对，其实主题是塔中的王子。

sentences.en: But of course, there is the question, which is what happened to them?
sentences.zh: 但当然，这里有个问题，那就是他们究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: Were they murdered?
sentences.zh: 他们是被谋杀的吗？

sentences.en: And if so, who murdered them?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，是谁谋杀了他们？

sentences.en: It is the absolute greatest mystery in English history, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这绝对是英国历史上最大的谜团，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's the one that everybody has heard of.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是人尽皆知的谜团。

sentences.en: It's the most romantic.
sentences.zh: 它最具浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: It's the one that sort of amateur historians still try to solve.
sentences.zh: 它是那种业余历史爱好者至今仍试图去解开的谜团。

sentences.en: And obviously, well, we shouldn't give away our answer, because we do have an answer, don't we?
sentences.zh: 显然，嗯，我们不应该泄露我们的答案，因为我们确实有答案，不是吗？

sentences.en: Collectively, I think we do.
sentences.zh: 大家集思广益，我想我们确实有了答案。

sentences.en: Is it fair to say that we've solved the mystery?
sentences.zh: 说我们已经解开了这个谜团，这样公平吗？

sentences.en: I think that might be going too far.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那样说可能有点过头了。

sentences.en: But I think we do, we have arrived at a consensus as to who we think did it.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们确实找到了，我们对究竟是谁干的达成了共识。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we should say that the focus is on, the title of this episode is Princes in the Tower, rather than Richard III or Henry VII or whatever,
sentences.zh: 我们应该说明重点是，本集题为《塔中的王子》，而不是《理查三世》或《亨利七世》之类的，

sentences.en: because we thought that would be a kind of interesting angle.
sentences.zh: 因为我们觉得那会是一个相当有趣的切入点。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, the Princes in the Tower, let's look at the eldest of them.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，塔中的王子，让我们来看看他们当中年纪最大的那一个。

sentences.en: The Edward who becomes Edward V.
sentences.zh: 也就是后来的爱德华五世。

sentences.en: And he is born on the 2nd of November, 1470.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1470年11月2日。

sentences.en: And it's not the most propitious circumstances, is it, for him?
sentences.zh: 对他的出生来说，这并不是最有利的环境，对吧？

sentences.en: No, he's born in, so he's born at a place called Cheneygates, which is the house of the Abbot of Westminster.
sentences.zh: 没错，他出生在……所以他出生在一个叫切尼盖茨的地方，那是威斯敏斯特修道院长的宅邸。

sentences.en: It's basically next to Westminster Abbey.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就在威斯敏斯特修道院旁边。

sentences.en: It's above the Croix gates, isn't it, I think?
sentences.zh: 我想它就在十字门上方，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: And his mother, so he is the son, we're in, yeah, 1470.
sentences.zh: 而他的母亲，所以他是……我们在，对，1470年。

sentences.en: He is the son of King Edward IV and his wife, Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 他是国王爱德华四世和妻子伊丽莎白·伍德维尔的儿子。

sentences.en: But he is born in sanctuary because his father has currently fled and is effectively in exile in the latest twist of the colossal Game of Thrones inspiring saga that is the Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 但他出生在避难所里，因为他的父亲当时已经逃跑，实际上处于流亡状态，这是作为《权力的游戏》灵感来源的宏大传奇——玫瑰战争中的最新转折。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so his wife, his queen, Elizabeth Woodville, has taken sanctuary there, as indeed she will do again subsequently.
sentences.zh: 所以他的妻子，他的王后伊丽莎白·伍德维尔在那里寻求了庇护，正如她后来确实还会再次做的那样。

sentences.en: And we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 我们等会儿会讲到这点。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of people claiming sanctuary in this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以这集里有很多人都在寻求庇护。

sentences.en: But you mentioned Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了玫瑰战争。

sentences.en: So let's look at Edward's two parents, Edward IV and Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们来看看爱德华的父母，爱德华四世和伊丽莎白·伍德维尔。

sentences.en: Let's look at Edward IV firSt. So, I mean, he has this kind of strange reign.
sentences.zh: 我们先来看看爱德华四世。我的意思是，他有着一种奇怪的统治生涯。

sentences.en: He comes to power and he rules and then he goes into exile and then he comes back again.
sentences.zh: 他掌权执政，然后流亡，接着又卷土重来。

sentences.en: And that's kind of unique, really, in the history of English kings.
sentences.zh: 在英国国王的历史上，这其实相当罕见。

sentences.en: So he is the son of someone who we mentioned in the Twelve Days of Christmas episode, Richard of York, who gave battle in vain.
sentences.zh: 所以他是我们在《圣诞十二日》那一集里提到过的人的儿子，也就是白白献出生命的约克的理查。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In a way, this is a kind of sequel to that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这是那段历史的续集，对吧？

sentences.en: Richard of York, who died at the Battle of Wakefield and his head was put on the gates and the crown and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 约克的理查在韦克菲尔德战役中战死，他的头颅被挂在城门上，还有王冠以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: With a paper crown and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 戴着纸王冠以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Margaret of Anjou.
sentences.zh: 安茹的玛格丽特。

sentences.en: And this.
sentences.zh: 还有这个。

sentences.en: So in a way, our story picks up straight after that.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们的故事紧接着那之后展开。

sentences.en: So Richard of York is the Yorkist claimant to Henry VI throne.
sentences.zh: 因此，约克的理查是亨利六世王位的约克家族宣称者。

sentences.en: So the English nobility is kind of divided between Lancastrians and Yorkists.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的英国贵族大致分为兰开斯特派和约克派。

sentences.en: And when Richard dies, his claim passes to his eldest son, who is Edward, Earl of March, I think he was before, who is this.
sentences.zh: 当理查死后，他的继承权传给了他的长子，我想他之前是马奇伯爵爱德华，也就是这个人。

sentences.en: So he's 18 years old when his father dies.
sentences.zh: 所以他父亲去世时他才18岁。

sentences.en: A scrapping lad.
sentences.zh: 一个好斗的小伙子。

sentences.en: He is extremely, he is the grandfather of Henry VIII, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他极其……他其实是亨利八世的祖父，对吧？

sentences.en: As it turns out.
sentences.zh: 事实证明确实如此。

sentences.en: So he's, if you listen to our Six Wives of Henry VIII podcast, he is very, very similar, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你听过我们的《亨利八世的六位妻子》播客，你会发现他其实非常非常相似。

sentences.en: His trajectory is very similar to Henry VIII, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 他的轨迹跟亨利八世非常相似，对吧？

sentences.en: You can definitely sort of see the genetic inheritance because he's huge.
sentences.zh: 你绝对可以看出基因的传承，因为他非常高大。

sentences.en: What is he, six foot four or something?
sentences.zh: 他有多高？六尺四英寸左右吗？

sentences.en: Which is absolutely colossal by the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时绝对是个庞然大物。

sentences.en: I think we mentioned this before.
sentences.zh: 我想我们之前提到过这点。

sentences.en: I think when and if William, Prince William becomes king, he's the only king who will be taller than Edward IV.
sentences.zh: 我想如果威廉王子未来成为国王，他将是唯一一个比爱德华四世更高的国王。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: May have got that wrong.
sentences.zh: 我也许记错了。

sentences.en: But Edward IV is, everybody says he is a very, very impressive person.
sentences.zh: 但大家都说爱德华四世是一个非常非常令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: And he's a massive lad, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他是个大块头，对吧？

sentences.en: He is a massive lad.
sentences.zh: 他确实是个大块头。

sentences.en: He likes his food, he likes his drink, and he likes his ladies.
sentences.zh: 他爱吃，爱喝，还喜欢女人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he likes fighting, and he's very good at fighting.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢打仗，而且很擅长打仗。

sentences.en: He's the sort of model, he's an alpha male, as Henry VIII was when his grandson will be when he's young.
sentences.zh: 他就像是个模范，是个阿尔法男，就像他的孙子年轻时那样。

sentences.en: He's a sort of a roistering, slaughtering, hard-living, hard-drinking, womanizing.
sentences.zh: 他是一个喧闹、好杀、纵情声色、酗酒、好色的人。

sentences.en: He's basically the guy from the University Rugby Club.
sentences.zh: 他基本上就是大学橄榄球俱乐部里的那种家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is.
sentences.zh: 没错，他就是。

sentences.en: He's the president of the kind of college sports society and all that.
sentences.zh: 他是那种大学体育协会的主席之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely he is.
sentences.zh: 对，他绝对是。

sentences.en: And quite quickly after his father's death, he turns it all around.
sentences.zh: 在他父亲死后不久，他很快就扭转了乾坤。

sentences.en: He wins a couple of battles, most famously the Battle of Tauton, which is the bloodiest battle ever fought on English soil.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了几场战役，其中最著名的是陶顿战役，那是英国本土上有史以来最血腥的战役。

sentences.en: And so by 1461, at the age of, basically by the time he's turned 19, he's on his way to becoming king, to kicking out the Lancastrians.
sentences.zh: 所以在1461年，当他基本上刚满19岁的时候，他已经在通往国王的道路上，准备把兰开斯特派赶出去了。

sentences.en: What does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: He captures Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 他俘虏了亨利六世。

sentences.en: And he doesn't kill him, does he?
sentences.zh: 但他没有杀他，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Because.
sentences.zh: 因为。

sentences.en: Which is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: Margaret Von Joux and their son, again, confusingly called Edward.
sentences.zh: 安茹的玛格丽特和他们的儿子——又是一个容易混淆的名字，也叫爱德华。

sentences.en: I mean, basically everyone's called Edward in this episode, so many apologies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这集里基本每个人都叫爱德华，实在非常抱歉。

sentences.en: So let's call him the Lancastrian Edward.
sentences.zh: 所以我们姑且叫他兰开斯特的爱德华吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: They've gone into exile.
sentences.zh: 他们已经流亡了。

sentences.en: So there's no point in killing Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 所以杀掉亨利六世毫无意义。

sentences.en: And in fact, he's a kind of an insurance policy because he's pretty de lally by this point.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他就像是一份保险单，因为到这个时候他已经有点神志不清了。

sentences.en: And so he's locked up in the tower.
sentences.zh: 所以他被关在了塔里。

sentences.en: He's looked after quite well, but he's kind of immured away.
sentences.zh: 他被照顾得相当好，但基本上是被软禁起来了。

sentences.en: And Edward sets about establishing the foundations of his regime.
sentences.zh: 而爱德华则着手建立他统治的基础。

sentences.en: It speaks well for Edward, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实对爱德华评价很好。

sentences.en: He doesn't kill Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 他没有杀亨利六世。

sentences.en: I don't think it does at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不这么认为。

sentences.en: I think it does.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是的。

sentences.en: No, I think it's pure politics because in due course.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这纯粹是出于政治考量，因为迟早有一天。

sentences.en: Well, of course he does kill him eventually.
sentences.zh: 当然，他最终还是把他杀了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I mean, I think that's reasonable.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我认为那是合理的。

sentences.en: After the.
sentences.zh: 在经历过。

sentences.en: No, I think Edward is completely ruthless.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为爱德华是个彻头彻尾的冷血动物。

sentences.en: Do you know who he looks like, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道他长得像谁吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Who?
sentences.zh: 像谁？

sentences.en: If you look at the portrait, he has the face of David Cameron.
sentences.zh: 如果你看那幅画像，他有着一张大卫·卡梅伦的脸。

sentences.en: Which, you know, there is something David Cameron-esque about him in that he's, I mean, he's ostensibly a kind of impressive figure.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他身上有一种大卫·卡梅伦式的特质，因为他表面上看起来是个相当厉害的人物。

sentences.en: He wins.
sentences.zh: 他总是赢。

sentences.en: You know, he's very successful at winning things, but ultimately he becomes a terrible failure.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在赢得胜利方面非常成功，但最终他却成了一个彻底的失败者。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I hope no spoilers there because.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希望这不算剧透，因为。

sentences.en: So Dave, if you're listening.
sentences.zh: 所以戴夫，如果你在听的话。

sentences.en: No, I agree.
sentences.zh: 不，我同意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There is something of that kind of ruddy cheeked.
sentences.zh: 确实有一种红光满面的感觉。

sentences.en: Posh.
sentences.zh: 有钱人的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think there is it.
sentences.zh: 我想确实有这么回事。

sentences.en: But I think, I think that Edward is, Edward IV is, is a very, very ruthless operator.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，爱德华——爱德华四世是一个非常、非常冷酷无情的操盘手。

sentences.en: I think if he has to kill people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果他必须杀人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He will.
sentences.zh: 他会动手的。

sentences.en: But he'll hug a husky first or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 不过他动手前会先拥抱一只哈士奇什么的。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 全都是这种调调。

sentences.en: So, so he, you know, he, I mean, he's, so he's ruling as a usurper basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以他，你知道，他，我的意思是，他是，所以他基本上是以篡位者的身份在统治。

sentences.en: And so his regime is inherently precarious.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的政权本质上是岌岌可危的。

sentences.en: There are lots of people who wish him nothing but ill.
sentences.zh: 有许多人对恨不得他去死。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，他就是那种在各种事情上挥霍巨额金钱的人。

sentences.en: Doublets.
sentences.zh: 紧身短衣。

sentences.en: Doublets.
sentences.zh: 紧身短衣。

sentences.en: Pies.
sentences.zh: 肉馅饼。

sentences.en: So Elizabeth Woodfield recognises that she has to look like a queen.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白·韦德维尔认识到她必须看起来像个王后。

sentences.en: So she does, she's very, very happy to spend money on looking like a queen, but otherwise she makes economies.
sentences.zh: 所以她确实这么做了，她非常非常乐意花钱来让自己看起来像个王后，但在其他方面她精打细算。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Of course, it's the problem that she brings all these kind of relatives that is the issue.
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于她带来了所有这些亲戚，这才是症结所在。

sentences.en: But she does bring one particularly, I think, tremendously cool relative, who's her brother,
sentences.zh: 但她确实带来了一个我认为特别酷的亲戚，那就是她的兄弟，

sentences.en: Anthony Woodville, who in due course will become a second girl.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·韦德维尔，他日后将成为第二个女孩。

sentences.en: Well, he's very clever, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他非常聪明，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's a great scholar and so on.
sentences.zh: 他是个伟大的学者等等。

sentences.en: He's a, but again, also a great sportsman.
sentences.zh: 他是一个，但同时也是个出色的运动员。

sentences.en: So he's a patron of Caxton, you know, who sets up the first printing press.
sentences.zh: 所以他是卡克斯顿的赞助人，你知道的，就是那个建立第一家印刷厂的人。

sentences.en: And he's actually translated a whole compendium of sayings of philosophers from the French that is one of the very first books that Caxton publishes.
sentences.zh: 而且他还从法语翻译了一整部哲学家名言集，这是卡克斯顿出版的最早的书籍之一。

sentences.en: But he also has this tremendous duel with a guy called the Bastard of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 但他也和一个叫勃艮第私生子的人进行了一场惊心动魄的决斗。

sentences.en: Do you know about this?
sentences.zh: 你知道这件事吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it's in, yeah, it's in, it's in Bart Van Leeu's book.
sentences.zh: 因为这在，是的，这在巴特·范·莱u的书里有。

sentences.en: It's in Thomas Penn's book of the Brothers York as well.
sentences.zh: 它也在托马斯·彭恩关于约克兄弟的书里。

sentences.en: They spent about 300 pages organising this massive tournament.
sentences.zh: 他们花了大约300页来筹办这场盛大的比武大会。

sentences.en: So the Bastard of Burgundy, which comes as no surprise to anyone who's heard the episode on the Burgundians, is the son of Philip, the good of Burgundy, who, as Bart reminded us,
sentences.zh: 所以勃艮第私生子——听过勃艮第那一集的人都不会感到惊讶——他是勃艮第好人菲利普的儿子，正如巴特提醒我们的那样，

sentences.en: tended to get a bastard every time he went on his travels.
sentences.zh: 他每次出行似乎都会留下一个私生子。

sentences.en: And yeah, they set up this kind of incredible showcase of jousting.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们举办了这场令人难以置信的比武展示。

sentences.en: Because these are the, you know, the Bastard of Antoine, the Bastard of Burgundy is the greatest jouster in Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 因为安托瓦内，勃艮第私生子是勃艮第最伟大的比武骑士。

sentences.en: And Anthony Woodville has the reputation as the greatest jouster in England.
sentences.zh: 而安东尼·韦德维尔则享有英格兰最伟大比武骑士的名誉。

sentences.en: And they have this kind of two day combat in London, where basically Anthony Woodville wins.
sentences.zh: 他们在伦敦进行了为期两天的对抗，基本上是安东尼·韦德维尔赢了。

sentences.en: I mean, Edward has to kind of step in and stop it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是爱德华不得不介入并阻止它。

sentences.en: And he's very, very cool.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常非常酷。

sentences.en: And he's on his, his, his tent.
sentences.zh: 在他的，他的，他的帐篷上。

sentences.en: He has this phrase, la nonchalance.
sentences.zh: 他有这样一句话，漫不经心。

sentences.en: So he's a, he's a kind of, he's a very cool guy.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个，他是一个非常酷的人。

sentences.en: That's very Cameroon, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常卡梅伦，不是吗？

sentences.en: To pursue the David Cameron analogy.
sentences.zh: 借用一下大卫·卡梅伦的比喻。

sentences.en: Oh, come on.
sentences.zh: 哦，得了吧。

sentences.en: No, I think he's, no, he's a kind of laid back, mellow, smart sportsman.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得他是，不，他是一个那种悠闲、温和、聪明的运动员。

sentences.en: But the thing though, Tom, is that he, okay, he is very, he's very impressive.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，汤姆，他，好吧，他是非常，他非常令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: He's very clever.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's very, you know, he's very cultivated and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他非常有修养，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But because he's from the Parvenu family, that stuff makes enemies.
sentences.zh: 但因为他来自暴发户家族，这种事情会树敌。

sentences.en: And the thing is, being a medieval king is all about, you don't have absolute power or anything like it.
sentences.zh: 问题是，作为一个中世纪的国王，这一切都在于，你并不拥有绝对权力或类似的东西。

sentences.en: What you have is this very complicated machine and these incredibly convoluted and elaborate and intricate networks of kind of regional loyalties and associations.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的是这个极其复杂的机器，以及这些极其错综复杂、繁复精细的区域忠诚和联系网络。

sentences.en: And you upset that at your peril.
sentences.zh: 如果你扰乱了这一点，后果自负。

sentences.en: You know, you need to keep that machine ticking along and basically divvying out the rewards, the offices, the lands, and making sure that everybody's happy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你需要让这台机器运转下去，基本上就是分发奖赏、职位、土地，并确保每个人都开心。

sentences.en: And, and, you know, I mean, you can go down one route and basically pick a side, kill the others or whatever, but then you have to do it really ruthlessly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的意思是，你可以选择一条路，基本上选定一方，消灭其他人什么的，但那样的话你必须非常冷酷无情。

sentences.en: Otherwise you have to keep things in balance.
sentences.zh: 否则你就必须保持平衡。

sentences.en: And you could argue that, I mean, we had quite a few questions about this.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，我的意思是，我们有很多关于这方面的问题。

sentences.en: Is Edward IV a failure because he basically allows the system to get out of balance?
sentences.zh: 爱德华四世是一个失败者吗，因为他基本上任由系统失衡？

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose I would argue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我会这样争辩。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Peter Davies, could you outline Edward IV's failures in allowing such factionalism to lead to regicide, the king who never lost the battle, but lost the war?
sentences.zh: 是的，那么彼得·戴维斯，你能概述一下爱德华四世在允许这种派系主义导致弑君方面的失败吗？那个从未输过战役却输了战争的国王？

sentences.en: I think, wouldn't you say, Tom, that such factionalism is inherent in the system?
sentences.zh: 我想，你不觉得吗，汤姆，这种派系主义是系统固有的吗？

sentences.en: You're always going to have different factions and keeping them in balance.
sentences.zh: 你总是会有不同的派系并保持他们的平衡。

sentences.en: I mean, Edward keeps them in balance, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上爱德华保持了他们的平衡。

sentences.en: Well, he makes one very big mistake, which in 14, what is it, 1470, 71, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他犯了一个非常大的错误，在14，是多少，1470年，71年，对吧？

sentences.en: When the factions get completely out of balance.
sentences.zh: 当派系彻底失衡的时候。

sentences.en: Which is, which is the backdrop for, for why his son, the future Edward V has to be born in sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 也就是，也就是他为什么他的儿子，未来的爱德华五世必须在避难所出生的背景。

sentences.en: And perhaps we should come to that after a break.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该在休息后谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史就是这样》。

sentences.en: We are proceeding at a somewhat glacial pace towards the story of the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 我们正以某种冰川般的速度推进塔中王子们的故事。

sentences.en: So we're just approaching the moment where the first prince is going to be born.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正接近第一位王子即将出生的时刻。

sentences.en: That's Edward V.
sentences.zh: 那是爱德华五世。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we ended the, just before the break, talking about Edward IV and factionalism.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我们在休息前结束了关于爱德华四世和派系主义的讨论。

sentences.en: And obviously, Edward IV is going to, he's in for a shock because he's offended the Earl of Warwick by marrying Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 很明显，爱德华四世将要遭遇震惊，因为他通过娶了伊丽莎白·韦德维尔冒犯了沃里克伯爵。

sentences.en: And this is about to, it's basically about to blow up in his face.
sentences.zh: 这即将，基本上要在他的脸上爆发了。

sentences.en: So in 1469, I think, you have the first real signs that the Earl of Warwick has, has basically allied with Edward's brother, George, who is the Duke of Clarence.
sentences.zh: 所以在1469年，我想，你有了沃里克伯爵基本上已经与爱德华的兄弟乔治（也就是克拉伦斯公爵）结盟的第一个真正迹象。

sentences.en: And George and Warwick feel very aggrieved at the intrusion of the Woodvilles into the kind of factional machine, and they're starting to get very restive.
sentences.zh: 乔治和沃里克对韦德维尔家族侵入派系机器感到非常不满，他们开始变得非常不安分。

sentences.en: And you start to get this sense that there's a kind of, there's a great cataclysm coming.
sentences.zh: 你开始有一种感觉，某种巨大的灾难正在来临。

sentences.en: And then it does come, doesn't it, in 14, what is it, 1470?
sentences.zh: 然后它确实来了，不是吗，在14，是多少，1470年？

sentences.en: Where Warwick basically changes sides, unbelievably, having been.
sentences.zh: 沃里克竟然难以置信地背叛了阵营，在此之前他是。

sentences.en: And as also does Clarence, false, fleeting, perjured Clarence, as Shakespeare has it.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯也是如此，正如莎士比亚所说，虚伪、多变、背信弃义的克拉伦斯。

sentences.en: So Warwick's treachery is, I mean, kind of understandable because Edward has basically shafted him with this marriage in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以沃里克的背叛，我的意思是，某种程度上是可以理解的，因为爱德华通过这桩婚姻在各方面基本上坑了他。

sentences.en: Clarence, I think, is less forgivable.
sentences.zh: 我认为克拉伦斯更不可原谅。

sentences.en: But anyway, so Edward, to his astonishment, I mean, it all kind of just melts away incredibly faSt.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，所以爱德华，令他吃惊的是，我的意思是，这一切都以令人难以置信的速度烟消云散了。

sentences.en: And Edward basically finds that he, despite being king for basically a decade, and actually playing the role of king quite well, he's not very popular.
sentences.zh: 爱德华基本上发现，尽管做了大约十年的国王，而且扮演国王的角色相当不错，但他并不是很受欢迎。

sentences.en: Support melts away.
sentences.zh: 支持烟消云散。

sentences.en: And he and his youngest brother, so there are three brothers, Edward IV, George, Duke of
sentences.zh: 他和他的小弟弟，所以有三个兄弟，爱德华四世，乔治，克拉伦斯公爵，

sentences.en: Clarence, who has sided with Warwick, and the younger brother, Richard, who'll become Duke of Gloucester.
sentences.zh: 他站在沃里克一边，还有小弟弟理查德，他将成为格洛斯特公爵。

sentences.en: In fact, is he Duke of Gloucester by this point?
sentences.zh: 事实上，到这个时候他是格洛斯特公爵吗？

sentences.en: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我记不清了。

sentences.en: So Richard, who is the youngest brother, doesn't betray Edward, sticks with him.
sentences.zh: 所以理查德，作为最小的兄弟，没有背叛爱德华，一直追随他。

sentences.en: And together they flee England, and they go to Burgundy, where Edward's sister, Margaret, has married Charles the Bold.
sentences.zh: 他们一起逃离英格兰，前往勃艮第，爱德华的姐姐玛格丽特嫁给了大胆查理。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Again, listeners may remember from the Burgundians.
sentences.zh: 同样，听众可能还记得勃艮第那一集。

sentences.en: They're taking place against the backdrop of this Franco-Burgundian rivalry.
sentences.zh: 他们正是在法兰西与勃艮第这种敌对背景下发生冲突。

sentences.en: So the French are backing a Lancastrian restoration with the Earl of Warwick, and the Burgundians
sentences.zh: 所以法国人支持兰开斯特王朝与沃里克伯爵的复辟，而勃艮第人

sentences.en: are basically offering Edward IV and his brother Richard sanctuary and time to kind of rebuild their forces.
sentences.zh: 基本上为爱德华四世和他的兄弟理查德提供避难所和时间来重建他们的军队。

sentences.en: So England is basically prey, to some extent, to the sort of great power ambitions of France and Burgundy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种程度上，英格兰基本上成了法国和勃艮第争夺大国雄心的牺牲品，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's with Burgundian support that Edward and Richard are able to return to occupy London.
sentences.zh: 正是在勃艮第的支持下，爱德华和理查德才得以返回并占领伦敦。

sentences.en: There's a terrible battle that is fought in Barnet, in North London, in the fog.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦北部巴尼特的雾中发生了一场惨烈的战斗。

sentences.zh: 非常浓的雾。

sentences.en: In the fog.
sentences.zh: 在雾中。

sentences.zh: 理查德在那里迂回包抄了沃里克。

sentences.zh: 有大屠杀。

sentences.zh: 沃里克被杀了。

sentences.en: Well, Warwick is very...
sentences.zh: 好吧，沃里克非常……

sentences.zh: 你知道吗，汤姆，我青少年时非常喜欢拥立者沃里克，自我……

sentences.en: Well, when I was kind of 11 or 12, when we did this at school, I was a very passionate admirer of Warwick the Kingmaker, and I've always felt he was very unlucky, because don't
sentences.zh: 好吧，当我大约11、12岁在学校学到这段历史时，我是拥立者沃里克的狂热崇拜者，我一直觉得他非常倒霉，因为难道

sentences.zh: 他的士兵在雾中把他们的一些盟友误认为是约克派吗？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And they open fire on them, and it all goes horribly wrong, and Warwick is kind of butchered by Yorkist soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们向他们开火，结果一切都糟糕透顶，沃里克被约克派士兵残酷杀害了。

sentences.en: To me, it always seemed a great tragedy that this very impressive magnate...
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这位非常了不起的权贵遭遇此下场似乎一直是一场巨大的悲剧……

sentences.en: And how do you feel now?
sentences.zh: 那你现在怎么看？

sentences.en: You're less of a fan.
sentences.zh: 你没那么崇拜他了。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: I don't...
sentences.zh: 我才不……

sentences.en: Well, I mean, they're all...
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，他们都是……

sentences.en: They're all brutal and horrible, weren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们都是野蛮而可怕的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they're all...
sentences.zh: 是的，他们都是……

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: But there's kind of horrible stories of people back in London waiting for news, and people start drifting back, and they've kind of lost their noses and, you know, eyes and
sentences.zh: 但伦敦有那种可怕的故事，人们在等消息，然后人们开始三三两两地回来，他们失去了鼻子，你知道，眼睛，

sentences.en: kind of horrible details.
sentences.zh: 还有一些可怕的细节。

sentences.zh: 这就是中世纪的战争，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 这就是中世纪的战争，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And has been reconciled with Edward, so it's...
sentences.zh: 并且已经与爱德华和解了，所以它是……

sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，乔治绝对不是本节目的朋友。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.zh: 我想你不会希望克拉伦斯做你的朋友。

sentences.en: Because you know he'd stab you in the back at some point.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道他在某个时刻会从背后捅你一刀。

sentences.en: He definitely would.
sentences.zh: 他绝对会。

sentences.en: Well, he's permanently aggrieved, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他一直在感到委屈，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got a...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有一种……

sentences.en: He really is the sort of...
sentences.zh: 他真的是那种……

sentences.en: The middle.
sentences.zh: 中间的。

sentences.en: The middle side.
sentences.zh: 中间派。

sentences.en: He has a terrible sense of entitlement and of victimhood, and everybody's against him.
sentences.zh: 他有一种强烈的权利感和受害者心态，觉得所有人都在跟作对。

sentences.en: He's like the one in The Godfather.
sentences.zh: 他就像《教父》里的那个。

sentences.zh: 他是弗雷多。

sentences.zh: 他其实是典型的中间兄弟，就像我认为弗雷多那样。

sentences.zh: 是的，我想他是。

sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否也是灵感来源，因为这一切在莎士比亚的书里都有。

sentences.zh: 而且阿尔·帕西诺还拍了一部关于理查三世的整部电影，所以谁知道呢？

sentences.zh: 他的儿子还小。

sentences.en: Tom, how are all the various Yorkist factions, how are they going to negotiate this youthful king?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，约克家族的各派势力将如何与这位年幼的国王周旋？

sentences.en: And that, I think, is a question that we should leave to answer until tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我想，这个问题我们还是留到明天再回答吧。

sentences.en: Oh, the tension.
sentences.zh: 噢，这紧张感。

sentences.en: It's such a cliffhanger, Tom.
sentences.zh: 真是个巨大的悬念啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: Huge, huge tension.
sentences.zh: 巨大，巨大的悬念。

sentences.en: I can't believe you could do this to the audience.
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信你对听众做出这种事。

sentences.en: But they love it.
sentences.zh: 但他们就爱这样。

sentences.en: Got to be done.
sentences.zh: 非做不可。

sentences.en: So we will see you tomorrow when we will talk about Princes in the Tower Part 2, when the princes actually will end up in the towers at laSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们明天见，我们将聊聊《塔中王子》第二部分，王子们终于要住进塔里了。

sentences.en: At least we've managed to get them born and alive.
sentences.zh: 至少我们成功让他们出生并活下来了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也算不错了。

sentences.en: It's like Tristram Shandy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 就像《项狄传》一样，对吧？

sentences.en: The whole thing.
sentences.zh: 整件事都是如此。

sentences.en: So we will see you then.
sentences.zh: 那我们到时候见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。
